comments.body:
=== STATUS: ROOT CAUSE PROVEN. FIX WRITTEN BUT **NOT LANDED** — IT REGRESSES TWO TESTS. ===

WHERE THE WORK IS. Local commit c207377b98 on branch `worktree-agent-a37f3385eb4a80049`'s sibling
worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1bf191c510431899`. Committed LOCALLY and
deliberately NOT pushed. It also carries the debug agent's `scratch_bug.md` / `scratch_churn.py`
reproduction so the analysis is not lost.

TWO PROCESS FAILURES TO RECORD, because both nearly cost the work:
 1. The debug agent died mid-task ("no progress for 600s") with the fix UNCOMMITTED.
 2. I then destroyed it. Running a mutation check, I reverted with `git checkout -- <file>` — which
    restores from HEAD, and the fix had never been committed. Both source files went back to
    pristine. Recovered by grepping the agent's JSONL transcript for the function body and
    re-applying it, then re-deriving the call-site wiring (which needed a function-local import of
    `drop_snapshot_echo_field_updates`, since `run_differs` does not import `reconcile_helpers` at
    module scope and the test loads modules by path).
    **LESSON: never `git checkout --` to undo a mutation on an UNCOMMITTED fix. Copy the file
    aside first, or commit before mutating.**

THE BLOCKER — the fix as written is TOO BROAD. With it applied, the diffing + orchestrate suites
report 2 failed / 406 passed, and both failures are about mutation COUNT:
  * `orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py::test_real_field_change_converges_after_one_pass`
    — "A genuine field change must produce mutation_count=1 on the [first pass]"
  * `orchestrate/test_reconcile_health_wiring.py::test_health_record_pass_called_after_apply`
    — "health.record_pass() must be called with local_mutation_cou[nt]…"

WHY THAT MATTERS AND WHAT IT MEANS. The fix's own justification is that "field sync for these keys
is already owned in BOTH directions by the binding-aware outbound and inbound differ phases that
run immediately afterwards". If that claim held universally, suppressing the snapshot differ's
`field_drift` emission could not change any mutation count for a GENUINE local field change. These
two tests say it does. So one of the following is true, and the next session must establish WHICH
before landing anything:
  (a) the claim is wrong — some genuine local field changes are carried ONLY by the snapshot
      differ's field_drift emission, and suppressing it is data loss, not de-duplication; or
  (b) the claim holds in production but these two tests drive a unit harness where the
      binding-aware phases do not run, so they are asserting the count the snapshot differ alone
      produces — in which case they pin the mechanism rather than the behaviour, and the honest fix
      is to rework them (preserving intent) rather than to weaken the suppression.
Do NOT resolve this by relaxing the assertions. This project has already found four tests that
encoded defects; the discipline is to determine whether a blocking test pins the BUG before
touching it, and to record the reasoning either way.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AND SHOULD NOT BE RE-DERIVED:
 * the root cause (`run_differs.py:222` passes the legacy `(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot)` pair to
   `differ.compute_mutations`, whose contract is `(local_state, jira_state)`) — see this ticket's
   description;
 * the suppression's unit test has TEETH, verified with a VALID mutation (make the filter a
   pass-through): exactly one cell fails, and the "a genuinely new remote key still plans its
   inbound create" cell keeps passing, so the suppression is correctly scoped to `field_drift`.
   NOTE my first mutation attempt was INVALID — it produced `reconcile_helpers.list(...)`, so both
   cells failed on an `AttributeError` rather than on the suppression's absence, which proves
   nothing. A mutation that goes red for the wrong reason is not a mutation check.
 * `make lint` and `make typecheck` both pass with the fix applied.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== OPEN QUESTION RESOLVED: (b). Both blocking tests pin the MECHANISM, not the behaviour. ===

Neither failure is data loss. Evidence, per test.

--- STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT: (a) is impossible at this call site ---
`reconcile.py:269-286` builds `prev_snapshot` from the persisted `.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json`
(an earlier FETCH) and `curr_snapshot` from `fetcher.fetch_snapshot`/`compute_snapshot`. BOTH are
pure remote Jira state; neither reads `local_tickets`. So the snapshot differ, at
`run_differs.py:222`, is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of observing a local field change. No genuine local
field change can be "carried only by" its `field_drift` emission, because it never sees the local
side at all. Genuine local changes are carried by `compute_outbound_mutations(local_tickets,
curr_snapshot, binding_store, ...)` — a different function reading a source the snapshot differ
never touches. That alone rules out (a); the two tests below explain what they were really pinning.

--- TEST 1: test_real_field_change_converges_after_one_pass ---
Instrumented the pre-filter mutation list in this exact harness. Pass 2 emits EXACTLY ONE mutation:

  outbound update DIG-20 payload={'summary': 'Original summary'}
                          provenance={'source':'differ','reason':'field_drift','local_id':'DIG-20'}

The fixture changes the summary from "Original summary" to "CHANGED summary" ON THE JIRA SIDE (the
acli stub returns issues_v2). The mutation the test counts pushes the OLD value BACK to Jira. It is
a revert of the remote edit, carrying the stale prev value — bug 727f itself, byte for byte.

The harness has NO local side: stderr shows `reconcile: ticket CLI exited 1 - local_tickets=[]`,
`RECON: outbound_differ total=0`, `RECON: inbound_differ total=0`. So there is no "genuine local
field change" in this test at all, and the binding-aware phases have nothing to act on. The test
asserts the count the snapshot differ ALONE produces.

Its docstring intent ("a genuine field change must be detected"; "a regression guard against
over-filtering") is legitimate and must be preserved — but the observable it chose is the defect.
The correct handling of a Jira-side field edit is INBOUND mirroring, not an outbound revert; that
is settled by ADR 0026's arbitrated inbound-mirrored scalar set and by b9b8 (HEAD, ae009443a9),
whose `test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py` cells assert precisely that a Jira-side edit with
local unchanged since baseline must NOT be emitted outbound.

--- TEST 2: test_health_record_pass_called_after_apply — a pure LIST-ALIASING ARTIFACT ---
This one has nothing to do with field_drift. The filter is a NO-OP here: instrumentation shows
`BEFORE 2 -> AFTER 2` (the stub differ returns two plain dicts with no provenance, so nothing
matches). The failure is `local_mutation_count=2, got 3`, i.e. the count went UP.

Discriminating experiment: replace `mutations = drop_snapshot_echo_field_updates(mutations)` with
an import-only no-op line, keeping the identical import. Test PASSES. So the import is innocent;
rebinding `mutations` to a NEW list is what changes the outcome.

Why: `_make_stub_differ` does `MagicMock(return_value=mutations)`, returning THE TEST'S OWN LIST
OBJECT. Downstream phases append IN PLACE, so at baseline the adopt/binding walk's extra
`(inbound, create) DIG-1` lands in the test's own list too. Proven by asserting inside the test at
HEAD~1 (no fix):

  DEBUG test-list-len=3 contents=[{'op':'create','key':'DIG-1'}, {'op':'update','key':'DIG-2'},
                                  Mutation(direction=inbound, action=create, target='DIG-1', ...)]

So `actual_count == len(mutations)` was comparing 3 == 3 against the SAME aliased object. The
assertion was vacuous — self-fulfilling for any number of appended mutations. The fix returns a new
list, breaks the alias, and exposes that the real count was always 3. Nothing is suppressed; the
third mutation existed before the fix and still exists after.

--- CONCLUSION ---
(b), and for test 2 more strongly than (b) predicted: its assertion never held teeth at all.
Reworking both, preserving intent, with the reasoning recorded in each docstring. Precedent for
this exact move is in b9b8's own commit message, which reworked
`test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` because it "asserted an observable no
production path emits".

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== FIX LANDED LOCALLY, GREEN, MUTATION-CHECKED. 727f AND d103 ARE ONE CHANGE. ===

WHAT CHANGED

`reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_echo_field_updates` is generalised and renamed to
`drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions`. It now drops BOTH arms whose correctness depends
on `local_state` genuinely being local state, matched on a `(direction, action, reason)` triple
AND a mandatory `provenance["source"] == "differ"` conjunct:

    ("outbound", "update", "field_drift")    <- 727f
    ("outbound", "create", "unbound_local")  <- d103

`differ.compute_mutations` is NOT touched; the suppression stays at the one call site so the
documented local-vs-jira contract survives intact for callers that honour it. Both
`differ.py`'s module docstring and `run_differs`'s docstring now record that the sole production
caller never migrated, and both carry an explicit note that the suppression must be REMOVED in
the same change if that caller is ever migrated (d103 acceptance criterion 3).

COMPLETENESS — the fix is exhaustive for this call site, not just for the two observables.
Fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair (a key only in prev, a key changed between prev and curr,
an unchanged key, and a key only in curr), `compute_mutations` can emit exactly three things:

    (inbound,  create, jira_new)        <- CORRECT here; preserved
    (outbound, create, unbound_local)   <- suppressed
    (outbound, update, field_drift)     <- suppressed

The differ's other local_state-dependent arms (`duplicate_local_id`, `ambiguous_local_binding`,
`dangling_jira_local_id`, and the absent-partner probes) are UNREACHABLE from a fetched snapshot,
exactly as d103 predicted: they read `local_id` / `jira_key` fields a fetched snapshot entry never
carries. So there is no residual wrong emission left behind at this call site.

RED -> GREEN. Four oracles, each seen RED against origin/main with a failure message naming the
mechanism, then GREEN:
 * diffing/test_snapshot_differ_stale_local_state.py
     ::test_a_converged_pair_plans_no_outbound_update_after_our_own_write   (727f, diff phase)
     ::test_a_key_that_left_the_fetch_window_plans_no_outbound_create       (d103, diff phase)
 * orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py
     ::test_real_field_change_converges_after_one_pass                      (727f, live path)
     ::test_a_key_absent_from_the_current_snapshot_never_reaches_create_issue (d103, live path,
       asserts at the TRANSPORT — client.create_issue is never called)
Positive controls, green throughout: the inbound create for a brand-new remote key still plans,
and an invariant SEED mutation survives (the seed deliberately reuses the `field_drift` reason
string, so a suppression keyed on reason alone would eat it).

MUTATION CHECKS — three, each verified to fail for the RIGHT reason:
 1. remove `("outbound","update","field_drift")` from the suppressed set -> exactly the two 727f
    oracles go RED with the phantom-echo message; both d103 oracles stay GREEN.
 2. remove `("outbound","create","unbound_local")` -> exactly the two d103 oracles go RED with
    the resurrect message; both 727f oracles stay GREEN.
 3. remove the `source == "differ"` conjunct -> exactly the seed-mutation control goes RED.
No mutation produced an AttributeError or an import failure, so none of these is the invalid kind
of mutation recorded on this ticket earlier.

GATES: `make lint` clean, `make typecheck` clean (407 files), `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler`
1808 passed. `run_differs.py` is 779 lines, under the 800 cap.

The fix was implemented by a subagent that never saw the oracles — the three test files were
moved out of its working tree and declared off-limits, and were byte-compared against a held-aside
copy after it finished. It was given the contract (the postconditions) and not the assertions.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF CHANGE 1209 BY A SECOND SESSION: NO ASSERTION WAS RELAXED. Checked
specifically because the operator's standing instruction on this ticket was 'do not resolve it by
relaxing the assertions', and because the fix necessarily touched two orchestrate cells that were
failing. Reviewed patchset 2 (13316a0ab1) against origin/main df41edcf25.

WHOLE-CHANGE ASSERTION LEDGER: 19 assert lines ADDED, 1 REMOVED. Net +18.

THE ONE REMOVAL, examined closely because this is exactly where a relaxation would hide.
Removed: 'assert result2["mutation_count"] == 1' from
orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py::test_real_field_change_converges_after_one_pass.
That assertion was PINNING THE DEFECT, not the behaviour its own docstring claimed. The fixture
changes the summary on the JIRA side only; the harness has local_tickets=[], so the single mutation
it counted was an outbound update carrying the STALE PREVIOUS value — a REVERT of the fixture's own
edit. Keeping it would have required the phantom to keep being emitted.

WHAT REPLACED IT — two assertions, and together they are strictly stronger than the one removed:
  * BOTH HALVES OF THE ORIGINAL INTENT ARE PRESERVED. The docstring's 'regression guard against
    over-filtering' now lives at pass 1: 'assert result1["mutation_count"] >= 1' — a key the
    reconciler has never seen is genuine work and must still be planned, so a suppression broad
    enough to swallow real work FAILS THERE. That is the guard the removed line was nominally
    providing, relocated to a pass where it is true.
  * A NEW STRICT ASSERTION AT PASS 2: 'assert result2["mutation_count"] == 0', with a failure
    message naming the mechanism ('the only thing the snapshot differ can emit here is an outbound
    update carrying the STALE previous value — a revert of the edit, not a sync of it'). == 0 is
    tighter than == 1, not looser.
  * The docstring records WHAT IT USED TO ASSERT, the instrumented evidence that this was wrong
    (the captured payload and provenance), and WHY zero planned work is correct here rather than
    lost work — a Jira-side field edit is mirrored inbound by the BINDING-AWARE differ (ADR 0026's
    arbitrated inbound-mirrored scalar set; ticket b9b8 and
    diffing/test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py), which needs a binding this snapshot-only
    harness never creates.

THE SECOND TOUCHED CELL WAS FIXED BY MAKING IT NON-VACUOUS, AND IT GAINED AN ASSERTION.
orchestrate/test_reconcile_health_wiring.py::test_health_record_pass_called_after_apply compared an
observed count against len(mutations) where _make_stub_differ returned THE TEST'S OWN LIST OBJECT,
which the diff phase appends to IN PLACE — so expectation and observation were the same object and
the cell passed for ANY number of appended mutations. The stub now returns a fresh copy (so the
expectation is a fixed value production cannot rewrite) and the snapshot is emptied for isolation,
matching what the sibling zero-mutation cell already relied on. A NEW assertion was added on top:
health.record_pass()'s count and the returned result['mutation_count'] come from different plumbing
and must agree.

CONCLUSION: this satisfies the constraint. One assertion that encoded the bug was inverted with its
intent preserved and its reasoning recorded in the docstring — the remedy AGENTS.md/handoff #6
prescribes for a test that pins a defect — and eighteen net new assertions were added around it.

compiled_state.description:
# The snapshot differ plans a phantom outbound update one pass after our own write

## Symptom

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing`
fails against the live Jira Data Center harness (run 30724309686). After an outbound title edit
has demonstrably landed on the instance AND become visible to a JQL search, a scoped dry-run
still plans
`{'direction':'outbound','action':'update','target':'RBJQFTF-1','local_id':'RBJQFTF-1'}`.
Index lag is excluded by construction (the cell waits for the search to reflect the new value).

## Proven root cause

`run_differs.py:222` calls `ctx.differ.compute_mutations(ctx.prev_snapshot, ctx.curr_snapshot)`,
feeding the PREVIOUS PASS'S REMOTE SNAPSHOT into the parameter `differ.py:5-11` defines as the
LOCAL source-of-truth state — the legacy argument shape that same docstring says was replaced.

`_compute_mutations_emit_both` (`differ.py:556-607`) then diffs every field outside
`EXCLUDED_FIELDS = ("local_id","rebar-id")` (`config.py:5`) and emits `(outbound, update)` with
`changed[field] = local_val`, i.e. the STALE prev value, with provenance `local_id = target`
(the Jira key) via `_derive_provenance` (`differ.py:130-131`) — the exact signature observed.

`reconcile.py:613` advances the prev snapshot with `shutil.copy2(curr_path, prev_path)`, i.e.
from the PRE-APPLY fetch, so an outbound write applied during pass N is invisible to `prev` at
pass N+1. One pass after our own write lands, prev != curr and the phantom is emitted. In a
dry-run `persist` is False, so prev never advances and it is re-planned forever.

Reproduced locally with no Jira:

    prev = {"K-1": {..., "summary": OLD, ...}}
    curr = {"K-1": {..., "summary": NEW, ...}}
    differ.compute_mutations(prev, curr)
    -> outbound/update target=K-1 local_id=K-1 payload={"summary": OLD}
    differ.compute_mutations(curr, curr) -> []

The mutation is inert at apply time: its payload is a bare field dict, not
`{"changed_fields": ...}`, so `batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict:100-103` resolves
`fields` to `{}` and `dispatch_one._update_one_scalar_update:640-650` issues an empty
`update_issue(key)`. Nothing changes remotely, so the mutation can never be satisfied — planned
every pass, counted against the `BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` cap of 10 (`mode.py:104-111`), inflating
`mutation_count` and making "converged" a lie.

Do NOT remedy this by correcting the payload shape: that would make it apply, reverting every
remote edit one pass later and flip-flopping forever.

## Why this is a defect and not intended behaviour

* `reconcile.py:609` states the invariant it breaks: "Advance prev snapshot so the next call
  converges to zero mutations."
* `differ.py:80-92` and the label branch at `differ.py:576-582` are a CLOSED fix (ticket
  robe-creek-zealot) for this exact mechanism, described verbatim there as a "spurious
  (outbound, update) echo". It was applied to labels only; every other field still churns. This
  bug is that fix's unswept sibling.
* Story 26de's contract, `differ.py:688-691`: "a write recorded as local-origin on pass N must
  not re-emit on pass N+1 even if the jira snapshot has not yet caught up."

## Blast radius

One cause explains all thirteen idempotence failures in harness run 30721408463, in BOTH
directions — the trigger is only "the remote issue changed since the last persisted fetch",
independent of which side changed it or which field.

## Fix

Drop the snapshot differ's field-drift `(outbound, update)` mutations at the
`run_differs.py:222` call site, keyed on their provenance (`source="differ"`,
`reason="field_drift"`). Do NOT change `differ.compute_mutations`'s documented local-vs-jira
contract: its unit tests legitimately exercise that contract with real local state, and other
callers may rely on it. For a bound pair, field sync in both directions is already owned by
`_run_differs_outbound` / `_run_differs_inbound`, which run immediately afterwards, so the
snapshot differ's field-drift emission there is pure noise.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A unit test drives the real diff phase with `prev` = a snapshot and `curr` = the same
   snapshot with one field changed, and asserts NO outbound update is planned. The test is seen
   RED before the fix and GREEN after, and returns to RED when the fix is reverted.
2. A genuinely new key (present in `curr` only) still yields its `(inbound, create)` — the
   edge-triggered inbound-create path the multi-page pagination cell depends on is unaffected.
3. `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the reconciler unit/integration suites pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

Finding 6 of ticket 5200 (a deleted DC issue plans an outbound CREATE instead of an inbound
probe) comes from the SAME emitter — a key present in prev-but-not-curr is read as "local has
it, Jira does not". It is a separate observable and is not fixed here.
compiled_state.title: Snapshot differ plans a phantom outbound update after our own write
